definitions.explanation: A compound word referring collectively to Buddhist temples and Shinto shrines. Used when discussing both types of religious sites together.

examples.japanese: ⟦{京都|きょうと}→京都：09484_kyouto⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{寺社|じしゃ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧。
examples.english: There are many temples and shrines in Kyoto.

examples.japanese: ⟦{正月|しょうがつ}→正月：01433_shougatsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{多|おお}く⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{寺社|じしゃ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{訪|おとず}れる→訪れる：07678_otozureru⟧。
examples.english: Many people visit temples and shrines during the New Year.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{地域|ちいき}→地域：01461_chiiki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{歴史的|れきしてき}→歴史的：05671_rekishiteki⟧な{寺社|じしゃ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{巡|めぐ}る→巡る：03930_meguru⟧⟦ツアー→ツアー：08285_tsuaa⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{参加|さんか}した→参加する：25408_sankasuru⟧。
examples.english: I joined a tour visiting the historic temples and shrines of this area.

notes:
USAGE:
The order {寺社|じしゃ} (temple-shrine) is the standard form. The reversed form {社寺|しゃじ} also exists and is interchangeable. Both refer to Buddhist temples (⟦{寺|てら}→寺：01676_tera⟧) and Shinto shrines (⟦{神社|じんじゃ}→神社：01620_jinja⟧) collectively.

In historical contexts, {寺社|じしゃ}⟦{奉行|ぶぎょう}→奉行：12661_bugyou⟧ was a Tokugawa-era magistrate overseeing temples and shrines.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {寺社|じしゃ}{仏閣|ぶっかく}: temples and shrines (more formal synonym)
- {寺社|じしゃ}{巡|めぐ}り: pilgrimage to temples and shrines
- {寺社|じしゃ}⟦{奉行|ぶぎょう}→奉行：12661_bugyou⟧: magistrate of temples and shrines (historical)
